title: Etale extensions commute with composition of finite-height valuations
statement: Let $F\subseteq E$ be a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. Let $A\subset F$ and $B\subset E$ be valuation rings [def-trf-valuation-ring] of finite height with fraction fields $F$ and $E$, respectively, such that $B\cap F=A$. Here height is the largest number of strict inclusions in a chain of prime ideals, and finite height means there are finitely many prime ideals. Put $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$ and $l=B/\mathfrak m_B$, where $\mathfrak m_A=A\setminus A^\times$ and similarly for $B$. Let $C\subseteq k$ and $D\subseteq l$ be valuation rings of finite height with fraction fields $k$ and $l$, respectively, such that $D\cap k=C$. If $A\to B$ and $C\to D$ are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], then the inclusion of the inverse-image rings $\{a\in A:\bar a\in C\}\to\{b\in B:\bar b\in D\}$ is etale. These inverse-image rings are the composed valuation rings in $F$ and $E$, respectively.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.2, printed pp. 11--12, together with Lemma 2.1.6.

proof.text: Write $R=\{a\in A:\bar a\in C\}$ and $S=\{b\in B:\bar b\in D\}$, and abbreviate $\mathfrak m_A=m$, $\mathfrak m_B=m'$, $\mathfrak m_C=p$, $\mathfrak m_D=p'$. Apply [lemma-nagata-composite-valuation-ring] twice: $R,S$ are valuation rings with fraction fields $F,E$, $m\subset R$, $m'\subset S$, and their residue restriction maps give $R/m=C$ and $S/m'=D$. All identifications here send an element to its actual residue. A valuation ring is local by the following direct check: its nonunits are closed under multiplication by ring elements, and for two nonzero nonunits $x,y$, either $x/y$ or $y/x$ belongs to the ring, so $x+y$ is a ring multiple of a nonunit. Thus the nonunits form an ideal, and every proper ideal lies in it. In particular $R,S$ are local. An element $r\in R$ is a unit exactly when its residue in $C$ is a unit: one direction follows by reducing its inverse, and the other by taking its inverse in $A$ and reducing. Hence the maximal ideals $n,n'$ of $R,S$ are the inverse images of $p,p'$, respectively, and $R/n=C/p$, $S/n'=D/p'$.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.2, notation paragraph; composition as in Lemma 2.1.4. Elementary locality and unit calculations supplied explicitly.

proof.text: The inclusions $A\to B$ and $C\to D$ are local. For example, $a\in A$ becomes a unit in $B$ precisely when $a^{-1}\in B\cap F=A$; the same argument uses $D\cap k=C$. The induced map $k\to l$ is therefore injective and agrees with the residue inclusion in the statement. By [def-weil-etale-morphism], the two assumed etale maps are unramified and locally of finite type. Apply [lem-trf-unramified-maximal-ideal-residue-criterion] to their closed points (the stalks of these local affine spectra are the rings themselves). It gives $m'=mB$, $p'=pD$, and finite separability of both $l/k$ and $(D/p')/(C/p)$. The inverse-image descriptions in Step 1 and the locality of $C\to D$ also show $S\cap F=R$ and $n'\cap R=n$.

proof.text: The $R$-module $S$ is torsion-free: if $0\ne r\in R$ and $rs=0$ in $S\subset E$, the field cancellation law gives $s=0$. Since $R$ is a valuation ring by Step 1, [lem-trf-valuation-torsionfree-flat] makes $S$ flat over $R$.

source.place: Tag 0ASJ, lemma-etale-extension-valuation-ring, algebraic value-group input; elementary denominator argument adapting Temkin Proposition 2.2.2.

proof.text: The affine etale/ring etale equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine] gives finite presentations for $B$ over $A$ and $D$ over $C$, hence finite sets of algebra generators. Choose $z_1,\ldots,z_r$ generating $B$ over $A$. For each $z_i$, Step 4 gives $c_i\in R\setminus m$ with $a_i=c_i z_i\in S$. Since every $c_i$ is a unit in $A$, still $B=A[a_1,\ldots,a_r]$. Consequently $m'=mB=m[a_1,\ldots,a_r]\subset R[a_1,\ldots,a_r]$: in any finite sum of products of an element of $m$ and a polynomial over $A$, each coefficient belongs to the ideal $m$ of $A$, and hence to $R$.

source.place: Tag 02GJ, lemma-etale-characterize; Temkin Proposition 2.2.2, finite-generation paragraphs.

proof.text: Lift a finite set of $C$-algebra generators of $D$ to $b_1,\ldots,b_t\in S$ using $S\to D$. For $s\in S$, express its residue as a polynomial in their residues with coefficients in $C$, and lift those finitely many coefficients to $R$. The resulting $q(b_1,\ldots,b_t)\in R[b_1,\ldots,b_t]$ has the same residue as $s$. Thus $s-q(b_1,\ldots,b_t)\in m'\subset R[a_1,\ldots,a_r]$ by Step 5. This proves the actual equality $S=R[a_1,\ldots,a_r,b_1,\ldots,b_t]$, including when either generator list is empty. In particular $S$ is a finite type $R$-algebra.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.2, final paragraph: residue generators and the inclusion of the coarse maximal ideal prove finite generation.

proof.text: For every $d\in m$ and $z\in B$ choose such $c$ for $z$; then $d/c\in m\subset R$ because $c$ is a unit of $A$. Hence $dz=(d/c)(cz)\in mS$. Using $m'=mB$ gives $m'=mS\subset nS$. The image of $nS$ under $S\to D$ is $pD=p'$, since $n\to p$ and $S\to D$ are surjective. The ideal $n'$ is exactly the inverse image of $p'$ and contains $m'$. Thus both $nS$ and $n'$ contain the kernel $m'$ and have the same image $p'$, so $nS=n'$. Moreover the residue extension $(S/n')/(R/n)$ is the finite separable extension $(D/p')/(C/p)$ of Step 2.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.2, maximal-ideal calculation; denominators supplied by Step 4 and quotient identifications by Step 1.

proof.text: Let $P=R[X_1,\ldots,X_{r+t}]$ and let $e:P\twoheadrightarrow S$ be evaluation at the generators of Step 6. Apply [lem-trf-valuation-finite-type-module-presentation] with base valuation ring $R$, finite type algebra $P$, and $P$-module $S$. This module is cyclic (generated by $1$ because $e$ is surjective) and is $R$-flat by Step 3. Hence $S$ is finitely presented as a $P$-module. Now [lem-trf-finite-presentation-surjective-module-kernel] applied to the surjective $P$-linear map $e:P\to S$ gives finitely many $P$-module generators of $\ker e$. As $\ker e$ is an ideal of $P$, those same generators generate it as an ideal. The evaluation map therefore presents $S$ as a polynomial algebra on finitely many variables modulo finitely many relations, exactly [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra].

source.place: Tag 053E, lemma-flat-finite-type-valuation-ring-finite-presentation, (2); Tag 0519, algebra.tex lemma-extension (5), for the module kernel. This supplies the finite-presentation check in Temkin Proposition 2.2.2 without using RG as an uncited black box.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-local-flat-unramified-etale] to the actual inclusion $R\to S$. The rings are local and the inclusion is local by Steps 1--2; Step 8 gives finite presentation, Step 3 flatness, and Step 7 both $nS=n'$ and finite separability of the residue extension. The criterion gives etaleness of $R\to S$, equivalently etaleness of its affine spectrum map. Step 1 already identified these two rings as the composed valuation rings in $F,E$. This proves every clause of the statement.
